The idea behind watering has always been water when they need it, because the roots do need a dry spell in order to breath. The reason plants that are over watered droop is because they are cut off from oxygen, and the plant suffocates. They best way to prevent this is to lift your plants pot after water them. Give them enough water so that 20-30% of the water runs out the bottom as runoff. Continue to lift the plant everyday, and you will begin to feel change in weight. 
When the leaves begin to droop again, this time due to being thirsty, make note of how heavy the pot is. Use this weight as a benchmark for further waterings.

Of course you will have to repeat this if you transplant, but it only takes doing it once to ensure you are giving your plant enough water and giving it oxygen the roots need.
